results.why: Both candidates score whether the operational setup (data sources, protocol, model/scale, comparison setting, outcomes) is reported completely enough to reconstruct the experiment, which is the same property as ML experiment-setup reporting transparency.
No candidate scores funding, conflicts of interest, sponsor role, or acknowledgment disclosure at all.

K28/K18 score methods-and-artifact detail sufficient to audit or reconstruct and K53 scores whether reproducibility/resource content is substantive rather than a promise, jointly the same reproducibility-readiness property, though the target additionally covers planned-vs-done and sharing-limit disclosure.
The structural candidates (K03, K07, K35) score whether one idea organizes the text, explicitly not length, and nothing scores concision, format, or venue length expectations.
No candidate scores software functionality, architecture, code quality/maintainability, or usability of a research software artifact.
Candidates about controls and comparisons (K26, K47, K25) score whether effects are isolated or shortcuts excluded, not whether the design's arms, units, allocation, and timing are described.

Reporting procedures in enough who/what/when/how detail to permit independent replication is exactly the operational-specificity/reconstructability property these two candidates score, in ML register.
No candidate scores venue aims-and-scope fit, originality eligibility, or baseline submission policy compliance.

Procedural and analytical detail sufficient for replication is the same reconstructability property scored by K18 and K28 (protocol, materials/data sources, comparison procedure, measurable outcomes).

K53 penalizes availability-upon-acceptance promises and dead links but rewards descriptive richness of the resource rather than actionable access, deposition, licensing, or availability statements, so the two would score abstracts differently.
No candidate scores dataset metadata, stewardship, intended-use limitations, or ethical/privacy and harm-avoidance guidance; K06 covers only scale and composition numbers.
K06 scores only concrete scale/composition of a newly built dataset, a fragment that omits provenance, collection timeframe, filtering rules, and representativeness of the final sample.
No candidate scores accessibility for readers with disabilities, inclusive language, or multilingual resources.

Hype-related candidates (K09, K40, K45, K46) score only claim inflation and would rate a measured but incomplete abstract highly, whereas the target also demands that background, methods, results, and conclusions all be accurately represented.

K40/K54 cover only evidence-proportionate claim language and K08/K15/K59 only limitation disclosure, each a fragment of a target that also requires prior-work contextualization, speculation marking, and implications without overreach.
K46/K16 score interpretability and precision of reported magnitudes but nothing scores defining primary versus secondary outcomes, their prioritization, or how and when they were measured.
